title: Does this feel like a prison yet?
author: kutan74

comments.author: Grandrcp
comments.body: ir looks unbelievable. Please tell me how did you creathe the scenario

replies.author: kutan74
replies.body: Thanks! I built it with a small modular prison kit, around 8-10 different 3D assets. I generated most of the models with Rodin AI, then assembled everything in Unreal Engine and did the materials, lighting and scene setup there.

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body:
I think there's something inherent to isometric/top view 3rd person perspective that makes prisons not really feel like prisons.  You can't feel the sense of confinement if you can see over the top of every cell, around every corner, even behind the walls.

So... does it look like a prison?  Yeah.  Feel?  Not really IMO.

replies.author: kutan74
replies.body: That's a fair point actually. The top-down camera definitely gives the player a lot of information. I'm thinking about occluding areas outside the player's line of sight to make it more confined.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body:
That sounds like a great solution.

I think the use of light will also play a huge role in that.  You've got something good started and I'd take it further... light and dark as functional gameplay elements, not just aesthetics.
